chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hafs al-Jawhari, whose title is al-Qurashi, from a man from the Kufis of our companions, who is called Ibrahim, that he said:
Hasan, peace be upon him, was asked about manliness, so he said: Chasteness with regards to religion, good dealing with regards to livelihood and patience during misfortunes.

key_terms.الْمَعِيشَة: Livelihood, sustenance, or way of living

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of manliness (Muru'ah) according to Imam al-Hasan?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Hasan (AS) elevates 'muru'ah' beyond physical bravery to encompass spiritual integrity ('iffah'), prudent resource management, and resilience ('sabr') in adversity. This trialing events. This triad reflects the Shia ethical ideal where inner piety and practical wisdom define true virtue, aligning with the concept of 'Insan al-Kamil' who balances worldly conduct with divine obedience. The emphasis on 'good estimation' in livelihood highlights the importance of avoiding both extravagance and miserliness, a key theme in Shia moral theology.

en.basel-kadem: 5.	With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Ali bin Hafs al-Jawhari, whose title is al-Qurashi, from a man from the Kufis of our companions, who is called Ibrahim, that he said:
Hasan, peace be upon him, was asked about manliness, so he said: Chasteness with regards to religion, good dealing with regards to livelihood and patience during misfortunes.
